chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what is killed by the stone and the pellet — can one eat from it? He said: No.

key_terms.البندق: Pellet/ball — a small round projectile, also killing by impact without cutting
key_terms.الحجر: Stone — a blunt projectile that kills by impact, not by cutting
key_terms.يؤكل: Can one eat — the question of permissibility (halal/haram) of consuming the game

ai.seo_question: Is game killed by a stone or pellet permissible to eat in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Sulayman ibn Khalid asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) whether game killed by a stone or a pellet — blunt projectiles that kill by impact rather than cutting — may be eaten. The Imam ruled that it may not. This reflects the jurisprudential principle that game must be killed by a sharp, cutting weapon (such as an arrow with a blade) to be permissible (halal) to eat; killing by blunt force renders the animal impermissible.
